The end of Fed hikes may be on the horizon but what about their effects on the economy?


According to TD, the peak impact from a rate hike occurs ~4 quarters later for GDP and ~6 quarters later for inflation.


In other words, what we see now is the effect of policy rates from mid-2022.


That means the peak impact of rate hikes on the economy has yet to be felt.


As Apollo’s Torsen Sløk notes, this will likely lead to further deterioration in credit conditions and lending growth.



Corporate bond spreads act as a proxy for overall macro concern among bond investors.


What are they saying?


Excluding a spike in March following the banking crisis, spreads have declined since October.


In fact, spreads are just as low now as they were before the banking failures.


This suggests investors believe the impact of macro headwinds on future earnings will be minimal.



Housing starts in the US fell by more than expected in June.


Building permits also declined against estimates for a modest gain.


Permits for single-family homes (SFH), however, increased by 2.2% and have been steadily rising which points to a rebound in SFH starts ahead (chart).


On the other hand, permits for multi-family units fell to the lowest since October 2020.

However, activist investor Starboard Value has taken a stake, and analysts believe boosting investment in Kenvue's consumer health brands could lead to revenue and earnings growth. At current valuations, Kenvue shares appear undervalued compared to peers, making it a potential buy for long-term investors.

title: Meet the 3.6%-Yielding Dividend King Stock That's Up 25% in 3 Months
description: Kenvue, a consumer health company spun off from Johnson & Johnson, has seen a 25.7% stock price increase in the last three months. This is partly due to solid earnings and guidance, as well as news of activist investor Starboard Value taking a significant stake in the company. While Kenvue has strong brands and a solid dividend yield, its valuation may be a concern for some investors.

title: Billionaire Ken Griffin Just Increased His Position in This Dividend Stock by 5,848%. Here's Why Now May Be a Great Time to Buy.
description: Billionaire Ken Griffin's hedge fund Citadel Advisors has significantly increased its position in Kenvue, a consumer health company with a 3.8% dividend yield. The article suggests Kenvue could be a compelling long-term investment due to its defensive and resilient business model.

title: 3 Dividend Stocks to Double Up on Right Now
description: The article discusses three dividend stocks worth considering: ExxonMobil, Kenvue, and Ford. It highlights the attractive dividend yields and financial positions of these companies, making them compelling income investment plays.

title: Listerine And Tylenol Maker Kenvue's Q3 Earnings: Revenue Miss On Weak Skin Health And Beauty Sales
description: Kenvue, the maker of Listerine and Tylenol, reported weaker-than-expected Q3 revenue due to a decline in its Skin Health and Beauty segment. The company expects full-year sales and organic growth to be at the lower end of its guidance range.

title: A Bull Market Is Here: 2 Super Stocks Down 21% and 30% to Buy Right Now
description: Uber and Kenvue are two stocks that the article suggests are undervalued and present good investment opportunities. Uber is the leader in the ride-hailing market and has shown impressive sales and margin growth, while Kenvue, a consumer health and beauty company, is trading at a discount to its peers and has the potential to improve its performance.

title: 3 Dividend-Paying Value Stocks to Buy Even If There's a Stock Market Sell-Off in 2025
description: The article recommends three dividend-paying value stocks - Lockheed Martin, American Water Works, and Kenvue - that are suitable for investors worried about a potential stock market sell-off in 2025. These companies have recession-resistant business models and emphasize dividend growth.
